title: [KDA] Support KDA packed decode
body:
## Motivation

KDA decode is **overhead-bound** at small batch. The existing flow inside `KDAAttnBackend.forward_decode` is:

```
causal_conv1d_update(mixed_qkv)
  → qkv.split([q_dim, k_dim, v_dim], dim=-1)
  → q.unflatten + q.unsqueeze
  → k.unflatten + k.unsqueeze
  → v.unflatten + v.unsqueeze
  → fused_sigmoid_gating_delta_rule_update(q, k, v, a, b, ..., is_kda=True)
```

For B=1, T=1 the actual math per layer is tiny (a few rank-1 state updates), but the wall-clock latency is dominated by:

1. **Python/PyTorch dispatch overhead** — `split` + 3× `unflatten` + 3× `unsqueeze` cost ~15-20µs of CPU per layer even though they only produce views.

title: fix: EPLB dispatch OOB when shared experts fusion enabled under DeepEP
body:
## Motivation


When --enforce-shared-experts-fusion and --init-expert-location are both enabled with DeepEP backend, biased_grouped_topk_gpu appends shared expert columns (value = n_routed_experts = 256) to topk_ids. The subsequent EPLB dispatch in _biased_grouped_topk_postprocess uses topk_ids as an index into the logical-to-physical dispatch table, which only has 256 entries (0-255). This causes a CUDA device-side assert (index out of bounds).

Fix: when fused shared experts are present under DeepEP, split off the shared expert columns before EPLB dispatch and concatenate them back after. Other code paths are unaffected (they take the else branch).

Tested on EP8 and EP16 with and without EPLB:

A request whose remaining prefill exceeds the prefill batch budget takes **all** of it. `add_chunked_req` allocates `min(rem_chunk_tokens, rem_total_tokens)` and `_update_prefill_budget` subtracts that from `rem_chunk_tokens`, leaving 0. ## Motivation

The current logprobs API only supports returning a fixed number of top-K token log probabilities per position (`top_logprobs_num`). This PR adds two new features:

1. **Top-P logprobs** (`top_logprobs_p`): Return the smallest set of tokens whose cumulative probability ≥ a threshold `p`. This is more semantically meaningful than a fixed-K, since it adapts to the sharpness of the distribution — returning fewer tokens when the model is confident and more when it is uncertain.
